issues.legal_issue: Cancelling agricultural tenancies over property held by charitable or religious institutions is a permissible classification under the constitutional guarantee of equality.
material_facts: The challenged law cancelled existing agricultural leases over land belonging to charitable or religious institutions, with an exception for qualifying landless poor tenants.
A commission report described difficulties in managing institutional lands, nominal rents, and possession by rich and powerful persons.

The record did not establish what rents were currently paid or what rents could be obtained under new leases, and the institutions could deal with resumed lands in different ways, including leasing them for better management.
issues.conclusion: The classification of institutional lands and their tenants as a distinct class was valid, and the challenge to the cancellation scheme on equality grounds failed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 prohibits class legislation, not reasonable classification. A classification must rest on an intelligible differentia distinguishing those grouped together from others and have a rational connection to the legislative object. It need not be scientifically perfect or logically complete, and a law is not invalidated by conjecture about how it may operate. Where the record contains no material showing that the law cannot achieve its object, the presumption that the law is valid prevails. The Court applied Article 14 and cited no earlier cases.

predicates.land_belongs_to_charitable_or_religious_: The agricultural land at issue was held by a charitable or religious institution.
predicates.cancellation_aims_at_better_management: The legislature made cancellation of existing tenancies part of a measure intended to improve management of institutional property.

predicates.evidence_does_not_show_objective_is_unac: The record did not establish that cancellation and subsequent management of the land could not achieve the legislative object.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns cancellation of tenancies over institutional land for better management, the classification may stand where management difficulties exist or the evidence does not show that the object is unachievable.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory distinction protecting tenants who meet a defined landholding limit, while allowing their tenancies to end if they do not purchase the land, does not make the scheme unconstitutional.
material_facts: The law defined a landless poor person by reference to the person's total land held as owner, cultivating tenant, or both, not exceeding two and a half acres of wet land or five acres of dry land.
A qualifying tenant with the required continuous tenancy was permitted to purchase the land at a prescribed portion of its prevailing market value in instalments.
If the qualifying tenant was unwilling or failed to purchase the land, the lease was to terminate.
The High Court considered that the distinction could cause unequal treatment between tenants with similar holdings.
issues.conclusion: The statutory definition and protection for landless poor persons were valid; the definition could not be enlarged, and termination when a qualifying tenant did not purchase the land was not inconsistent with the protection.
issues.legal_principle: Section 82 of the Andhra Pradesh Charitable and Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act, 1987, defines the landless poor category and provides for qualifying tenants to purchase land. The legislature may determine who is exempt from a law. A law's validity is not assessed by fortuitous consequences arising from particular circumstances.

predicates.qualifying_tenant_is_given_purchase_oppo: The qualifying tenant was given an opportunity to purchase the leased land.

issues.definition: The protection and purchase opportunity for a tenant within a defined landholding limit are valid when the tenant is given the opportunity to purchase the land.

issues.legal_issue: Differences in tenancy rights arising under different regional tenancy laws do not create distinct classes for the purpose of cancelling tenancies over institutional land.
material_facts: Tenants in different regions were subject to different tenancy legislation and could have different rights under those laws.
The challenged cancellation applied to their agricultural holdings under charitable or religious institutions.
The Court found that, with respect to holdings under those institutions, the tenants fell into the same relevant category.
issues.conclusion: The different rights arising under the regional tenancy laws did not invalidate the common classification of tenants holding land under charitable or religious institutions.
issues.legal_principle: For Article 14 classification, persons may be treated as a single class where the circumstance relevant to the challenged measure is common to them. Section 82 of the Andhra Pradesh Charitable and Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act, 1987, concerned tenants' holdings under institutions, and differences in rights under other enactments were not material to that classification. The Court cited no earlier cases.

issues.definition: Different regional tenancy rights do not defeat a common classification when the tenancies concern land held by the same kind of institutional landlord.

issues.legal_issue: A cancellation provision does not displace ownership that a tenant has already acquired after ownership-conferral proceedings have been completed.
material_facts: A petitioner relied on a provision of the Telangana tenancy legislation that could confer ownership on tenants.
The Court stated that if the proper proceedings had been adopted and had reached their logical end, the tenant would become the owner.
The Court distinguished that situation from one in which proceedings had not ended and the tenancy continued.
issues.conclusion: The cancellation provision did not apply where proceedings had reached their end and ownership had vested in the tenant; it applied where proceedings had not ended and the tenancy remained in force.
issues.legal_principle: Section 38-E of the Andhra Pradesh (Telangana Area) Tenancy and Agricultural Land Act, 1950, concerns conferment of ownership rights. Section 82 of the Andhra Pradesh Charitable and Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act, 1987, applies to a tenancy that continues, but not to a case in which the tenant has already become the owner through completed proceedings. The Court cited no earlier cases.

issues.legal_issue: The possibility that cancellation of a tenancy may cause hardship does not by itself establish that the law deprives the tenant of a livelihood.
material_facts: The law cancelled existing leases over agricultural land held by charitable or religious institutions for the purpose of better management.
The petitioners argued that tenants' livelihoods would be deprived.
The Court observed that the record did not establish that the land was the tenants' only land or that cultivating it was their only occupation.
issues.conclusion: The livelihood challenge failed because possible hardship to some tenants did not establish that the law deprived them of their livelihood.
issues.legal_principle: Article 21 was invoked, but the Court held that possible hardship is not sufficient to show deprivation of livelihood where the record does not establish that the affected land was the tenant's only land or sole occupation. The object of the measure was better management of institutional property. The Court cited no earlier cases.

predicates.tenancy_is_cancelled_for_better_manageme: The tenancy was subject to cancellation as part of a measure intended to improve management of institutional property.
predicates.evidence_does_not_show_land_was_sole_liv: The evidence did not establish that the land was the tenant's only land or that cultivating it was the tenant's only occupation.

issues.definition: A livelihood challenge fails when cancellation serves better management and the evidence does not show that the land was the tenant's sole livelihood.

issues.legal_issue: The constitutional provision concerning immunity for certain enactments does not apply when the State has not invoked that immunity.
material_facts: The petitioners relied on Article 31A in arguing that tenants were entitled to compensation.
The State had not undertaken an exercise to give the enactment immunity from challenge under Articles 14 and 19.
issues.conclusion: The Article 31A contention was unfounded and did not affect the case.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A provides immunity for certain enactments from challenge under Articles 14 and 19. The Court held it irrelevant where the State had not undertaken to invoke that immunity. The Court cited no earlier cases.

predicates.article_31a_immunity_not_invoked: The State did not undertake to invoke constitutional immunity for the enactment.

issues.definition: The immunity contention is irrelevant to a constitutional challenge when the State has not invoked that immunity.

issues.legal_issue: The cancellation of a tenancy prevents a claim based on the tenancy's inheritance from preserving the tenancy.
material_facts: The petitioners argued that the tenancies were inheritable and that tenants could not be deprived of them without compensation.
The challenged measure cancelled the leases themselves.
issues.conclusion: The inheritance contention did not prevent cancellation, because the question of inheritance arose only if the leases continued to exist.
issues.legal_principle: Where the lease itself is validly cancelled, a claim that the tenancy is inheritable does not preserve it. The Court considered the cancellation provision in Section 82 of the Andhra Pradesh Charitable and Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act, 1987, and cited no earlier cases.

predicates.challenge_to_tenant_cancellation: A party challenged the application of a tenancy-cancellation measure to land held by a tenant.
predicates.tenancy_is_inheritable: The tenancy was claimed to pass by inheritance.

issues.definition: An inheritance claim cannot preserve a tenancy after the lease itself has been cancelled.
